newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: RPT - PHILIPS MAY POST 1996 LOSS - PAPER.
newsitem.headline: RPT - PHILIPS MAY POST 1996 LOSS - PAPER.

text.p: Dutch electronics firm Philips could actually post a 1996 loss if it opts to book the costs of severing its ties with troubled German unit Grundig against last year's result, De Volkskrant newspaper said on Saturday.

"The 1.8 billion guilders set aside by (management board chairman Cor Boonstra) for restructuring is not enough. He needs around 700 million extra to throw German subsidiary Grundig out of the house," it said.
Philips was not immediately available to comment on the report on Saturday.

In 1995 the company posted a 30 percent rise in net income from normal operations to 2.68 billion guilders. In the first nine months of 1996, net income from normal operations dwindled to 804 million from a year-earlier 1.67 billion.
The company said then it would take a charge of approximately one billion guilders before tax in the fourth quarter.
Philips said earlier this month it was deconsolidating Grundig to become a passive minority (32 percent) shareholder.
It is currently in talks with Grundig to unravel its contract to pay an annual 50 million guilder dividend to the Max Grundig Foundation, which owns the other 68 percent of Grundig.
In addition the companies were in dispute over the payment by Philips of Grundig's losses and several other contractual obligations, De Volkskrant said.
Philips did not expect the dispute to be settled before the announcement of 1996 results on February 13, but it could set aside an average amount of 700 million guilders, the paper said.

Together with the 800 million guilders needed to restructure its consumer electronics division and the one billion guilders set aside for lighting, household appliances, media, PolyGram and monitor components, this provision would wipe out the contribution made by Philips' healthy units, the paper said.
